comment: The miss was treating LayerNorm count and activation as near-independent advantages. In this tiny, momentum-free SGD regime, the winning interaction is: leaky/rectifier plus residual transport and enough normalization (D); then a moderately deep smooth net with one normalization stage (E); then a shallow residual smooth net (B). A's extra early norms did not overcome its deeper plain stack, while C combined the deepest smooth stack with no normalization and was worst. K1039 misled me by making rectifier-vs-smooth activation too dominant; K1006 correctly warned that LN evidence is conditional, but I failed to apply the depth/residual condition. A review of 56 low-rate XOR records showed repeated reversals of simple LN-count or residual-only rules.
hypothesis: For 2-feature XOR with 256 steps of momentum-free SGD at lr around 3e-4, rank by an interaction score rather than additive LN count: (1) leaky/ReLU receives a strong advantage; (2) residual transport helps shallow or moderately deep stacks; (3) one strategically placed LN can rescue a smooth stack, but extra LN does not compensate for a deeper plain stack; (4) deep smooth zero-LN stacks are last. Applied here: D (leaky, residual, 3 LN) < E (SiLU, 1 LN, moderate depth) < B (GELU, shallow residual) < A (GELU, deeper plain despite 2 LN) < C (deep SiLU residual, zero LN), matching the revealed order. This is a task- and budget-scoped rule, not a universal architecture law.
